newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lukoil plans new convertible bond issue this year.
newsitem.headline: Lukoil plans new convertible bond issue this year.

text.p: Russia's biggest oil company OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil plans a new issue of bonds convertible into its shares, probably this year, company vice-president Nikolai Tsvetkov said on Thursday.

"An issue is planned, and further issues are being worked on. By the end of the year would be realistic," he told a news conference. He said it was premature to name terms but said these had improved now that LUKoil had received an international credit rating. It is rated BB- by Standard & Poor's.

A $200 million bond, convertible into shares in 2002, was oversubscribed in April. LUKoil also made two issues of convertible bonds in 1995, mainly bought by U.S. oil company Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO), which ended up with 7.99 percent of LUKoil.
LUKoil, which is expanding both in Russia and abroad, and this week made a $125 million private placement of a bond.

Tsvetkov said Chase Manhattan was advising LUKoil on a separate issue of bonds backed by oil exports, but a planned Eurobond issue would have to wait until the company has prepared accounts to international standards.

KPMG has prepared financials for 1994 and 1995, but 1996 figures are still being worked on, and accounts should be ready by early 1998, he said. LUKoil is Russia's and one of the world's largest oil companies by reserves.
